In pigs, protection by SMEF was accompanied by suppression of a stress and inflammatory program without detectable leukocyte accumulation, consistent with an epithelial origin, and not by restoration of pump or mitochondrial transcripts. The results fit an intervention that acts on the function of existing molecules rather than on their expression.

items.title_en: Modeling and Detecting Downward Causation in Disease Transmission
items.title_zh: 疾病传播中向下因果的建模与检测
items.abstract_en: We compare two epidemic models: the deterministic SIR (Susceptible-Infected-Recovered) model and the maximum-entropy-based DyMES (Dynamic Maxent across Entwined Scales) framework. In contrast to the widely used SIR model, the recently proposed DyMES model incorporates both top-down and bottom-up mechanisms and thus can capture local responses to global behavior. We simulate both models in three disease scenarios using parameter values drawn from the literature and analyze trends in the epidemic trajectories. Increasing the strength of downward causation lowers the peak but extends the time taken to return to the initial state, changing the trajectory from an SIR-like rise and fall to an epidemic with a long tail. By combining the Maxent inference procedure and top-down causation, the DyMES model predicts the probability distribution of disease incidence across population sub-aggregates.

items.title_en: RiboCouple links RNA backbone generation to sequence design through a learned interaction topology
items.title_zh: RiboCouple 通过学习到的相互作用拓扑将 RNA 骨架生成与序列设计联系起来
items.abstract_en: Designing RNAs with prescribed structures is central to RNA engineering. Backbone-first approaches generate geometry before sequence assignment, yet how to transfer relational information to sequence design remains unclear. We introduce RiboCouple, which infers a probabilistic residue-pair state from backbone geometry, recycles pair probabilities through a second pass and transfers them to sequence decoding as soft attention biases. On 550 generated backbones, pair-type decoding achieved joint refolding validity of 45.1 percent versus 33.5 percent for a matched topology-free decoder. In another 110-backbone cohort, replacing aligned pair states with statistics-matched donor states reduced validity from 46.4 percent to 21.4 percent, demonstrating that decoding depends on backbone-aligned relational information. Before external refolding, pair-confidence ranking enriched validity to 59.6 percent in the top 248 and transferred to other generators; on a 94-chain temporally held-out native-backbone benchmark, pair-coupled decoding improved secondary-structure agreement. These findings establish backbone-inferred interaction topology as an intermediate representation connecting backbone generation, sequence decoding, and candidate prioritization.

items.title_en: A latent space thermodynamic model of cell differentiation
items.abstract_en: Inferring the governing dynamics of differentiation that capture cell state evolution remains a central challenge in single-cell biology. We present Single-Cell Latent Space Dynamics (scLSD), a thermodynamics-inspired framework that models cell differentiation as evolution on a learned Waddington landscape in latent space. scLSD jointly infers a low-dimensional cell state, a differentiable potential function governing developmental flow, and a local entropy term that associates with cellular plasticity. Using a neural ordinary differential equation, scLSD reconstructs continuous differentiation trajectories from time-ordered single-cell data. Across diverse developmental systems, scLSD accurately recovers lineage hierarchies, predicts fate commitment for unseen cell types, and outperforms existing trajectory inference approaches in directional and cell fate prediction accuracy. In silico gene perturbations reveal how individual regulators reshape the landscape, and the proposed entropy measure is informative of plasticity in development and cancer.

items.title_en: How much is enough? Optimising sampling frames for genomic surveillance of Escherichia coli and Klebsiella spp. bloodstream infections - a retrospective study
items.abstract_en: Background: Optimising sampling frames for genomic surveillance of E. coli and Klebsiella may support interventions to mitigate bloodstream infections (BSIs), but approaches to estimating sample size and how these relate to bacterial population diversity at multiple genetic levels (strain/plasmid/antimicrobial resistance genes [ARGs]) are lacking. Methods: Using systematically collected, regionally-stratified, whole genome sequencing data from a 6-month genomic survey of English E. coli/Klebsiella BSI isolates (n=1,939; NEKSUS), we used Bayesian approaches to estimate the sample sizes required to capture genetic diversity at strain- (MLST, fastBAPS clusters), plasmid- and ARG-levels, using two diversity measures: 'coverage' (i.e. proportion of the bacterial population/plasmids/ARGs represented by features observed in the sample), and the number/proportion of unique features observed at varying surveillance sample sizes. Our method is available as a user-friendly R Shiny application, EpiSENTRY (https://01a0c3dd-90d2-e597-58a5-51391a468387.share.connect.posit.cloud/). Findings: Randomly sampling 1,400 E. coli/Klebsiella BSI isolates each achieved [≥]80% coverage of bacterial lineages and ARGs (i.e. capture features constituting [≥]80% of the population) at 95% certainty, but captured lower proportions of unique features (28% MLSTs, 59% fastBAPS clusters, 19% plasmid subcommunities, and 57% ARGs for E. coli; 49%, 87%, 50% and 83% for Klebsiella, respectively). Sample sizes required for 80% coverage of E. coli plasmid populations were higher than MLSTs (1,928 [95% CrI: 1,837-2,025] vs 1,351 [1,230-1,472]), while for Klebsiella, estimates were lower for plasmids (1,115 [1,052-1,181] vs 1,422 [1,331-1,515] for MLSTs). Lower sample sizes adequately captured 80% coverage of fastBAPS clusters and ARGs (649 [575-727] and 27 [23-30], respectively, for E. coli; 113 [84-145] and 83 [72-96] for Klebsiella), due to feature-specific frequency distributions. Klebsiella BSIs were more diverse than E. coli, with sampling 10.9% vs 3.2% of total annual BSIs in England needed to reach 80% MLST coverage. Plasmid populations and Klebsiella MLSTs were region-specific, emphasising the need for regionally-representative sampling. Interpretation: Bayesian analysis facilitates estimates of context-specific genomic surveillance sample sizes. Cost-effective targets for coverage require further optimisation.

items.title_en: Human Islet Transcriptomics in Type 2 Diabetes Reveals Conserved Dysfunction Axes and a Candidate Gene Panel
items.abstract_en: Background. Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2D) involves progressive pancreatic beta-cell dysfunction, but conserved islet programs require cross-cohort and single-cell validation. Methods. We integrated four human islet transcriptomic cohorts using differential expression, random-effects meta-analysis, Hallmark scoring, and module scoring. To test generalizability without reusing held-out outcomes, modules were re-derived from three cohorts and scored in the fourth in rotating study-level cross-fitting, with expression- and detection-matched random gene-set nulls. Machine-learning performance in GSE164416 was estimated by nested stratified 5-fold cross-validation with DEG calling and feature selection repeated within each outer training fold. An annotation-compatible score was tested in GSE50244, and beta-cell validation used GSE221156. Results. Cross-fitted IsletDysfunctionScore effects were positive in all four held-out cohorts (d = 0.39-1.36; pooled Hedges g = 0.905, 95% CI 0.501-1.309, p = 1.14 x 10^-5, I2 = 5.5%). Matched gene-set null testing supported effects beyond random expectation in two cohorts. Nested machine learning yielded AUC = 0.960 (bootstrap 95% CI 0.900-0.997); GABRA2 and ENSG00000284653 were selected in all outer folds. The external 8-gene consensus-pool score achieved AUC = 0.907 (DeLong 95% CI 0.818-0.996), but its fixed threshold did not transfer. In GSE221156, the single-cell dysfunction-score analog increased and BetaIdentitySecretion decreased in T2D; ImmuneStress was nominally increased but did not survive false-discovery correction across the single-cell score family. Conclusions. Human T2D islets show a reproducible stress/identity-loss framework that generalizes directionally under study-level cross-fitting and beta-cell-resolved validation. The candidate panel is a research transcriptomic signature requiring further validation.

items.title_en: Kidney research (APOL1 and FSGS) violates new ethics of 'race': Medicontextualism debunks bad science undermining healthcare
items.abstract_en: BACKGROUND Apolipoprotein L1 (APOL1) gene variants, associated with increased risk of focal segmental glomerulosclerosis (FSGS) and kidney failure, were found in US patients of West African heritage but absent in European and Taiwanese patients--Taiwan having one of the highest rates of kidney disease. Methodological limitations could affect these findings. A history of segregation in the southern US led researchers to propose biologic 'race' as the root of disparity in kidney disease. We hypothesized that persistent US segregation racializes health, education, employment, and access. METHODS First, for cross-cultural clarity, we defined terms to orient international colleagues to the semantics of socially constructed 'race' (in Europe) and racialization of health (in the US). Second, we removed 'race correction' from estimated glomerular filtration rate under more equal conditions of US veterans. Third, we used data re-analysis to suggest alternative mechanisms for links between the medicontexts of socially constructed 'race', apolipoprotein L1 gene variants, and racialized kidney disease. RESULTS There was no 'racial' disparity in kidney failure under more equal social conditions. Geographically localized "ancestry markers" may proxy for 'race'. 'Colorism' may be associated with apolipoprotein L1 variants linked to medicontextual (e.g., pigmentary) genes that may be tracked with a polygenic risk score (PRS) for structural racism. CONCLUSIONS Under equal conditions, comparable outcomes should be the expected norm for all, regardless of socially constructed 'race', ethnicity, or nationality. Medicontextualism locates disparity between socially constructed categories in disparate social conditions. Ending silence on 'race' debunks bad science (BS) and suggests potential insights from a "structural-racism PRS". International collaboration to discourage misuse of socially constructed 'race' in healthcare and medical research is an actionable Population Health initiative with potentially high impact but low effort and cost.

items.title_en: Predicting HPV/p16 Status and Molecular Subtypes from Histopathology Slides using Deep Learning in Vulvar Squamous Cell Carcinoma
items.title_zh: 利用深度学习从组织病理学切片预测外阴鳞状细胞癌的HPV/p16状态和分子亚型
items.abstract_en: Vulvar squamous cell carcinoma (VSCC) comprises three prognostically distinct molecular subtypes: human papillomavirus (HPV)-associated, HPV-independent/p53-wildtype, and HPV-independent/p53-abnormal. Classification requires p16/p53 immunohistochemistry, which consumes tissue and is often incomplete in retrospective cohorts. We investigated whether deep learning could predict HPV/p16 status and molecular subtypes directly from routine hematoxylin and eosin-stained whole-slide images. Using features extracted with H-optimus-1, we developed two attention-based multiple-instance learning models: HERA, predicting HPV/p16 status, and HERMES, predicting the three molecular subtypes. Models were developed on 644 patients from three Dutch VSCC cohorts and tested on 286 patients from two independent cohorts. In independent testing, HERA achieved an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.84 (95% CI 0.75-0.91), with specificity 0.93, negative predictive value 0.94, and sensitivity 0.68. HERA-predicted groups reproduced the prognostic separation of HPV testing (log-rank p<0.001). HERMES achieved a macro-average AUC of 0.70 (0.66-0.75), with good discrimination for HPV-associated (0.80) but limited separation of HPV-independent/p53-abnormal (AUC 0.68) and HPV-independent/p53-wildtype (AUC 0.63). HERMES-predicted classes reproduced the prognostic hierarchy, with 5-year recurrence rates of 14.0% (HPV-associated), 31.1% (HPV-independent/p53-wildtype) and 43.3% (HPV-independent/p53-abnormal) (p=0.0051). Highly attended tiles showed basaloid cells and koilocytotic-like atypia in HPV-associated tumors, keratinizing nests with desmoplastic stroma in HPV-independent/p53-abnormal tumors, and well-differentiated keratinocytes with spongiosis in HPV-independent/p53-wildtype tumors. HERA could assign HPV/p16 status to large retrospective VSCC cohorts lacking ancillary testing, without consuming tissue, enabling HPV-stratified outcome analyses. Before such use, external validation of its discrimination and calibration across scanners and populations is required. HERMES suggests that molecular subtype information is encoded in hematoxylin and eosin-stained slides, but requires improved distinction between the HPV-independent subtypes.

items.title_en: Sex Differences Across the Donor Heart Offer-to-Outcome Pathway: A Linked National Cohort Study
items.title_zh: 供体心脏从分配提议到结局路径中的性别差异：一项关联全国队列研究
items.abstract_en: Background: Sex differences occur across heart transplantation, but where they become apparent between donor-heart offers and post-transplant outcomes is uncertain. Methods: We linked UNOS STAR Q2 2025 candidate, donor, transplant, and PTR match-run data across pre- and post-2018 eras. Analyses included 51,970 listing episodes, 1,388,553 actual offers, and 38,417 recipients and evaluated access, conditional final acceptance, donor profiles, severe predicted heart mass (PHM) undersizing (ratio <0.86), treated rejection, and 365-day survival. Results: Transplant access increased in both sexes without evidence of sex-by-era modification (P=.133). Offers made to female candidates had higher adjusted conditional final-acceptance probabilities in both eras (interaction P=.172). After recipient-size standardization, severe PHM undersizing among realized offers remained less frequent for women than men pre-policy (28.9% vs 38.3%) and post-policy (25.5% vs 35.4%); acceptance of undersized offers was not lower for female candidates (three-way interaction P=.800). The threshold donor composite showed modest differences that reversed direction across eras. Adjusted treated rejection remained higher among women (male vs female OR, 0.667; 95% CI, 0.589-0.756), including after post-policy cPRA adjustment (OR, 0.678; 95% CI, 0.583-0.790). Adjusted post-policy 365-day survival was 91.0% in women and 92.3% in men; the sex difference did not change across eras (-0.64 percentage points; 95% CI, -1.97 to 0.68; P=.341). Conclusions: Sex-associated patterns were stage-specific and multidirectional. The final-graft PHM difference was already evident among realized offers after size standardization and was not explained solely by lower acceptance of undersized offers for female candidates. Women nonetheless had more treated rejection, while short-term survival differences did not change significantly across eras. Transplantation performance should be assessed separately across offer exposure, acceptance, matching, and outcomes.

items.title_en: Caesarean section in Bangladesh, 2012-13 to 2025: facility birth, the private sector and small-area geography
items.title_zh: 孟加拉国剖宫产（2012-13至2025年）：机构分娩、私营部门与小区域地理
items.abstract_en: Background: In Bangladesh, caesarean section rose from one in five births in 2012-13 to one in two in 2025. We asked how much of this rise came from more facility births, a move to private facilities, and changing rates within sectors. Methods: This repeated cross-sectional study used Multiple Indicator Cluster Surveys from 2012-13, 2019 and 2025 (26,539 recent mothers). A Kitagawa decomposition split the rise into parts. For 2025, we mapped caesarean use among facility births in 2,720 clusters and examined modelled travel time. Results: The caesarean rate rose from 19.5% (95% CI 18.1 to 20.9) to 52.0% (50.7 to 53.2). More facility births made up 82.8% (78.9 to 87.7) of this 32.5 point rise and the move to private facilities 12.6% (10.1 to 15.0). In a one-step version, place of birth made up 94.7% (90.7 to 98.9). The private caesarean rate rose from 79.1% to 86.1%, while the public rate fell from 38.7% to 33.5%. Among private first births, which rarely follow a previous caesarean, the 2025 rate was 4.8 points (0.3 to 10.2) above the 2012-13 model's prediction. The 2025 private rate was 85% to 87% in every wealth group. Longer travel time was linked with fewer caesareans, mainly through fewer facility births. Among private-sector births, travel time was not linked with caesarean (prevalence ratio 0.99 per 10 minutes, 0.97 to 1.01). Caesarean use among facility births clustered geographically; the private share of births in nearby clusters, not household factors, accounted for much of this. Conclusions: In accounting terms, most of the rise came from births moving into facilities, mostly private ones, where caesarean was already common. The data cannot show how many caesareans were needed. If 2025 sector mix and rates persist, more facility births would keep raising the national rate.

items.title_en: Community-Level Wastewater Surveillance of Nicotine Biomarkers Tracks Cardiovascular Disease Burden and Myocardial Infarction
items.title_zh: 社区层面尼古丁生物标志物污水监测可追踪心血管疾病负担与心肌梗死
items.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Tobacco smoking is the largest modifiable contributor to cardiovascular disease (CVD), yet population-level surveillance still relies on self-reported and retail data, which are subject to measuring bias and lag. Urinary and salivary cotinine quantify individual tobacco exposure, but no analogous, objective metric exists at the community level. Wastewater-based epidemiology (WBE) has transformed surveillance of infectious diseases and illicit drug use; whether the same approach can yield a community-level signal of CVD risk is unknown. OBJECTIVE: The primary objective of this study is to track community-level wastewater nicotine biomarkers and evaluate potential correlations with relative CVD burden in El Paso, Texas. METHODS: We integrated wastewater nicotine biomarker surveillance with electronic health record (EHR) data across four sewersheds in El Paso, Texas. Twenty-four-hour composite influent samples were collected monthly (June 2024 to May 2025; n=48) and quantified by liquid chromatography tandem mass spectrometry for five nicotine metabolites. Cotinine, nornicotine, and trans-3-hydroxycotinine (3HC) were detected in 91.6 to 100% of samples, whereas tobacco-specific nitrosamines were below limit of detection. CVD cases (January 2021 to December 2024) were obtained from the Paso del Norte Health Information Exchange and mapped to sewersheds by residential ZIP code using ArcGIS. At the sewershed level, population normalized nicotine mass loads tracked the proportional burden of atherosclerosis/ischemia/infarction and heart failure. Across the sewersheds, monthly 3HC mass load and the nicotine metabolite ratio (NMR) were strongly and specifically associated with incident ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) (3HC vs. STEMI: rho=0.893,p=0.012), without parallel associations for non-ST elevation or old myocardial infarction. CONCLUSIONS: To our knowledge, this is the first demonstration that integrating wastewater nicotine surveillance with EHR data can reveal community-level 3HC and NMR as specific indicators of incident STEMI. Our findings indicate wastewater surveillance as a novel, objective tool to inform cessation policy and CVD prevention

items.title_en: USFDA Oncology Drug Approvals from 2014- 2025: Comparing non-immunotherapy and immunotherapy approvals, their endpoints, and their efficacy.
items.title_zh: USFDA 2014—2025年肿瘤药物批准：非免疫治疗与免疫治疗批准、其终点及疗效比较
items.abstract_en: In the United States the Food and Drug Administration (FDA), and in Europe, the European Medicines Agency (EMA) are responsible for regulatory approvals of anti-cancer therapeutics. We examined regulatory approvals by both agencies in the period between 2014 and 2025 and compared immunotherapy and non-immunotherapy approvals for the treatment of cancer. We asked whether the approvals were similar in terms of trial size, endpoints, and development time. We present the data based on the FDA approvals given that the US agency has approved some therapies either rejected by or yet to be approved by the EMA. Beginning with the approval of pembrolizumab for melanoma in 2014 through early 2025 we identified 143 immunotherapy and 211 non-immunotherapy approvals. In the first few years the time to approvals of immunotherapies was markedly less but over time the duration has approached that of non-immunotherapies - with durations of 2079 and 2357 days in 2024/2025 due largely to a median trial size of 461 and 698 participants. Surrogate endpoints have overwhelmed overall survival as the primary endpoint for approval, and we find that with non-immunotherapies only a median of 60% of the benefit predicted from progression/disease/recurrence/event-free survivals translates to overall survival, significantly less than the 99% of the surrogate benefit translated to overall survival for immunotherapies. While the FDA and EMA approval portfolios are very similar, the EMA is on the whole more skeptical/conservative in its approvals. The last decade has seen substantial advances, but much remains to be accomplished against a formidable foe. The size and duration of trials need to be addressed and meaningfully reduced and the validity of surrogates defended.

items.title_en: Trajectories and characteristics of pain in the first year after spinal cord injury: a TRACK-SCI study
items.title_zh: 脊髓损伤后第一年疼痛的轨迹与特征：一项TRACK-SCI研究
items.abstract_en: Chronic pain affects most individuals with spinal cord injury (SCI) and frequently impairs daily function, and nearly half experience neuropathic pain. Neuropathic pain is commonly thought to develop months after injury and to persist once established. These views rest on classifying each patient as having neuropathic pain or not, although patients often report several pains. The same binary label is the usual target of prognostic and biomarker studies that aim to predict life-limiting pain. We tracked up to three of the worst pains per interview from injury to one year in 140 TRACK-SCI participants, using the DN4 interview (DN4i, threshold 3). Within three days of injury, half of all pain areas and three quarters of participants met the threshold, and pain-area prevalence changed little over the year. Individual pains, however, often changed. Only a third remained above the threshold throughout, one third resolved or fluctuated, and pains in the same person often followed different courses. At more than half of interviews with several pains, one pain met the threshold while another did not, so that the patient's classification depended on the pain considered. We therefore derived a threshold-free Pain Composite Score from the DN4i items and pain intensity. The items formed a single dimension, and the composite was associated with sleep and mood interference whereas the binary classification was not. Neuropathic pain after SCI thus appears early, does not invariably persist, and differs between a person's pains, and graded pain-level measures may offer a more stable target for predicting life-limiting pain.

items.title_en: Relevance-Based Prediction: A Transparent, Patient-Specific Approach to Predicting Medical Outcomes
items.title_zh: 基于相关性的预测：一种透明、面向个体患者的医学结局预测方法
items.abstract_en: Accurate prediction of individual medical outcomes is essential for optimizing treatment allocation amid rising costs, coverage denials, and limited clinical resources. Traditional predictive models, including linear regression and neural networks, rely on average effects and cannot tailor predictions to the specific circumstances of individual cases. We present relevance-based prediction (RBP), a model-free and task-specific method that predicts outcomes as weighted averages of observed cases, with weights determined by a rigorously defined and theoretically justified measure of relevance. Unlike model-based methods that rely on fixed calibrated parameters, relevance-based prediction revisits the original data for each prediction and customizes both the cases and variables used. We illustrate RBP by applying it to predict opioid treatment outcomes and demonstrate that it provides case-specific insights unavailable from conventional models, including how each prior case informs a prediction, how each variable affects each predictions reliability and value, and how reliable each prediction is before it is made. These individualized insights may prevent misleading average-based decisions and reduce harmful or suboptimal treatment.
items.abstract_zh: 在成本上升、保险拒付增多和临床资源有限的背景下，准确预测个体医学结局对优化治疗分配至关重要。传统预测模型（包括线性回归与神经网络）依赖平均效应，无法针对个案的具体情形量身定制预测。我们提出基于相关性的预测（RBP）：一种无模型、任务特异的方法，它将结局预测为已观测病例的加权平均，权重由严格定义且有理论依据的相关性度量确定。与依赖固定校准参数的模型化方法不同，RBP在每次预测时都重新检视原始数据，并自定义所使用的病例与变量。我们以阿片类药物治疗结局预测为例展示RBP，证明它能提供传统模型无法给出的个案洞察，包括每个既往病例如何影响某次预测、每个变量如何影响每次预测的可靠性与价值，以及预测在做出之前有多可靠。这些个体化洞察有助于避免误导性的、基于平均值的决策，减少有害或次优的治疗。
items.highlight_zh: 用病例加权的无模型预测，让每个预测都可解释、可追溯
items.digest_zh:
1. 研究了什么问题：医疗资源紧张、费用上涨，如何为每位患者准确预测治疗结局、合理分配治疗，变得非常关键。但常用的线性回归、神经网络等模型依赖「平均效应」，给出的是人群层面的规律，很难贴合某个具体病人的特殊情况，也难解释「为什么这么预测」。
2. 用了什么方法：作者提出「基于相关性的预测」（RBP）。它是一种无模型、针对具体任务的方法：预测值不是由一组固定参数算出，而是取已观测病例的加权平均，权重来自一个被严格定义并有理论依据的「相关性」度量。每次做新预测时，方法都会重新回到原始数据，自己挑选最相关的病例和变量。
3. 有什么结果：作者以阿片类药物治疗结局预测为示例，显示RBP能给出传统模型没有的个案级洞察：某个既往病例如何影响这次预测；每个变量如何影响该次预测的可靠性与价值；以及在预测做出之前，这次预测本身有多可靠。
4. 为何重要：临床决策若只依据群体平均值，可能对个体产生误导。RBP的透明性和个案适配性，有望帮助医生避免「平均化」的错误决策，减少有害或不理想的治疗选择，同时让预测过程可追溯、可解释。

items.title_en: Source-water salinity measured by electrical conductivity in Bangladesh, 2025: a nationally representative cross-sectional survey
items.title_zh: 2025年孟加拉国通过电导率测量的水源盐度：一项全国代表性横断面调查
items.abstract_en: BackgroundIn coastal Bangladesh, saline drinking water has been linked to raised blood pressure. The 2025 Multiple Indicator Cluster Survey (MICS) measured electrical conductivity (EC), a salinity indicator, in source water, but its report gave no population counts or district estimates. ObjectivesTo estimate how many people live in households whose tested source has high EC, and to describe patterns by place, household characteristics, source type and arsenic. MethodsEC was measured in source water of 6,040 households in 64 districts, February to June. In 14.5% of households the tested source was not the main drinking-water source. Primary outcomes were EC above 1,500 and 3,000 {micro}S/cm, survey risk classes that are not health-based standards. Estimates were survey weighted; comparisons were observational. ResultsEC exceeded 1,500 {micro}S/cm in 5.3% of households (95% CI 4.7 to 5.9), about 9.0 million people, including 1.8 million above 3,000 {micro}S/cm. Coastal-zone districts held 26% of households but 70% of those above 1,500 {micro}S/cm. Shares varied little by wealth or in households with young children or pregnant women. Nationally, deep tube wells more often had high EC because most are coastal. In the coastal zone, deep and shallow wells had similar shares (16.1% and 17.9%). After district adjustment, EC was about 18% lower in deep wells (geometric mean ratio 0.82, 0.73 to 0.92). Within upazilas (restricted sample) it was 0.93 (0.80 to 1.07). Arsenic above 10 ppb was more common where EC was high, but this link weakened after district adjustment. ConclusionsMillions of people live in households whose tested source has high EC, mostly in coastal and south-central districts. Deep wells had modestly lower EC after geographic adjustment, but the difference shrank within upazilas and depended on the handling of implausibly low readings. The findings support measuring EC alongside arsenic, with documented meter calibration.

items.title_en: Patient-keyed aggregation of public cancer genomic data imports clonal hematopoiesis into solid-tumor mutation matrices
items.abstract_en: Large-scale reuse of public cancer genomic data begins by pooling studies into one patient-by-gene matrix, keyed on the patient. Records held under one patient identifier need not come from the same kind of specimen: three clonal-hematopoiesis studies in cBioPortal deposit blood normals sharing patient identifiers with tumors deposited elsewhere, so a patient-keyed merge records a hematopoietic clone as a tumor mutation. We linked 1,282,483 coding calls in 140 genes from 483 studies to patients, classified each by specimen type, and rebuilt the matrix with and without blood-derived calls. Blood normals supply 1.7% of calls but concentrate: 52.8% of patients flagged DNMT3A-mutant, 21.3% of TET2 and 19.7% of CHEK2 have no tumor-derived call in that gene, against 0.4% for TP53. Those calls carry a hematopoietic gene spectrum and, in TP53, hematopoietic allele fractions. The artifact reaches 65 further cohorts, almost all solid-tumor studies, exceeding one patient in ten in fifteen of them, and tracks the share of patients with a paired blood normal, not the disease (r = 0.994, 45 cancer types). Correction lowers the pan-cancer DNMT3A rate by 45% and moves survival estimates further than chance removal of the same patients would. Two filter lines applied before aggregation remove it.

items.title_en: Cholesterol Paradox: Multi-point Heart Failure Prediction from Lipid Panels in Electronic Health Records
items.title_zh: 胆固醇悖论：基于电子健康记录中脂质检测组合的多点心力衰竭预测
items.abstract_en: In cardiovascular medicine, low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) is the main lipid marker used in routine screening to assess cardiovascular risk and guide preventive treatment and dietary changes. An increasing number of studies have recently documented the cholesterol paradox: patients with or at risk of heart failure (HF) often have unexpectedly low levels of LDL-C despite leading to cardiovascular diseases. This paper examines how well retrospective lipid panel measurements, supplemented with apolipoprotein B (ApoB), can predict an initial heart failure (HF) event in several pre-diagnosis time windows, using age-matched patient data from Electronic Health Records (EHRs). This retrospective study uses lipid profiles from multicenter nationwide EHRs from the All of Us Research Program. We apply machine learning and explainable AI (SHAP) to lipid-based prediction and to interpret cholesterol contributions to the diagnosis of first heart failure (HF). One experiment predicts the diagnosis of HF in 36 months; the other distinguishes HF patients from people who have never been diagnosed with cardiovascular disease. A baseline lipid panel that includes ApoB predicts the first HF event up to 36 months in advance, achieving an AUC of 0.624 in men and 0.627 in women. Compared to a group of the same age without previous cardiovascular disease, a lipid profile including ApoB predicts a first HF event with a substantially higher AUC: 0.937 for men and 0.925 for women. Shapley value analyses suggest that higher triglycerides and lower HDL and LDL levels are linked to subsequent HF events, with LDL appearing as the strongest yet counterintuitive predictor. ApoB ranks second in importance; in males, higher ApoB is associated with a greater risk of HF, unlike LDL. In general, the study highlights an unexpected association with LDL and emphasizes the prognostic utility of sex-specific metabolic indicators (TG, HDL) for HF using routinely collected clinical data.

items.title_en: Low-risk Features of Emergency Department Patients on a Sepsis Pathway: A Retrospective Cohort Study
items.abstract_en: Introduction For adult emergency department (ED) patients initiated on a sepsis care pathway, we sought to identify patient factors associated with favorable clinical and operational outcomes that could help identify patients potentially eligible for sepsis care de-escalation. Methods We conducted a retrospective cohort study using an electronic health record (EHR) data query from five hospitals in New York City (2022-2024). Multivariable logistic regression models were used to evaluate association of patient demographics, clinical characteristics, and ED diagnoses with four favorable reference outcomes: shorter hospital length of stay (HLOS), no intensive care unit (ICU) stay, survival to discharge, and no sepsis adjudication according to institutional quality-of-care standards. Results Among 9,443 ED visits, 45.9% of participants were 36C, absence of hypotension, WBC count 4,000-15,000/uL, and lactate <2.0mmol/L linked to multiple outcomes. Age 18-49 years had the strongest association for HLOS <72 hours (adjusted odds ratio (aOR) 3.48, p<0.01) and survival to discharge (aOR 3.15, p<0.01); lack of severe diagnosis had the strongest association for no ICU stay (aOR 2.74, p<0.01); and ED diagnosis other than sepsis or infection had the strongest association for no sepsis adjudication (aOR 8.82, p<0.01). WBC count 4,000/uL to 15,000/uL was the only factor associated with all four outcomes (aORs 1.24-1.70). Patients with a primary ED diagnosis of infection other than pneumonia had more favorable outcomes than those diagnosed with sepsis or pneumonia. Conclusion Several patient factors may help identify lower risk patients who could be targeted for sepsis care de-escalation after a sepsis pathway has been initiated, although the relevant factors differ by outcome. Further research is needed to evaluate the performance of these factors in prospectively identifying patients most likely to experience favorable outcomes.

items.title_en: Glucoregulatory and Inflammatory Trajectories in Pregnancy with Obesity: Secondary Analysis of a Randomized Exercise Trial
items.abstract_en: Objective: To evaluate moderate-intensity exercise effects on glucoregulatory and inflammatory markers in pregnant women with obesity. Methods: Secondary analysis of the Expecting Study (NCT02125149) included 263 sedentary pregnant women with pre-pregnancy BMI [≥]30kg/m2 randomized to exercise (EX, n=157) or standard-of-care (SoC, n=106). Fasting biomarkers were assessed at 12.14{+/-}0.50, 24.19{+/-}0.68, and 36.03{+/-}0.58 weeks ' gestation. Linear mixed-effects models evaluated intervention and gestational effects at 24-36 weeks. Exploratory repeated-measures continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) included 18 participants (SoC=6, EX=12), evaluating 24-h/temporal glycemia and exploring inflammatory marker associations. Results: Insulin, C-peptide, HOMA2-IR, HOMA2-%B, IL-6, and TNF- increased with gestation, while HOMA2-%S and CRP decreased (all p 95% valid wear time; glycemia remained normoglycemic. By 36-weeks, SoC-metrics declined in 24-h and nocturnal glucose and time-in-range (TIR), with increased time-below-range (all p<0.022). TIR was inversely associated with IL-6 at 24-weeks (-0.23 [95%CI: -0.43,-0.02] p=0.035), and mean amplitude of glycemic excursion positively with TNF- at 36-weeks (0.02 [95%CI: 0.00,0.04] p=0.033). Conclusion: Exercise did not modify mid-to late-gestation fasting glucoregulatory or inflammatory profiles. High CGM-adherence and preliminary indications of distinct longitudinal glycemic patterns support further CGM evaluation in antepartum behavioral interventions.

items.title_en: Exploratory brain-wide analyses predicting binge drinking: A machine learning and targeted causal inference pipeline in two adolescent cohorts
items.abstract_en: Background: A sizeable literature has found that neuroanatomical differences predict alcohol use outcomes in adolescence. However, due possibly to small samples and inconsistent/limited methodologies, it is still unclear which specific morphometric features are most predictive and if they are also causally implicated in binge drinking onset. Methods: To differentially predict abstinence from binge drinking by age 16-17, a SuperLearner ensemble algorithm was fit to structural and diffusion MRI features at age 9-10 in the Adolescent Brain and Cognitive Development cohort (ABCD). A separate model was fit using the National Consortium on Alcohol and NeuroDevelopment in Adolescence (NCANDA), in which the MRI predictors were measured later (ages 12-17) but the developmental outcome (binge drinking by age 18) remained similar. The top ten predictors were extracted from each model, and the causal role of these features scrutinised using targeted maximum likelihood estimation (TMLE). Results: Predictive performance in ABCD was poor (AUC=.585) but was stronger in NCANDA (AUC=.695). There was little overlap in predictive feature rankings between the cohorts. TMLE did not reveal a causal effect of the top ten morphological predictors on binge drinking in either cohort. Conclusions: No evidence was found for causal contributions of any discrete macrostructural/microstructural brain feature in late childhood or adolescence to binge drinking. Using more sophisticated metrics of brain structure and function may yield better insights. Adding to previous evidence from youth cohorts, neuroanatomy may have greater predictive value for identifying those at risk of adolescent binge drinking when measured in adolescence, rather than late childhood.

items.title_en: Machine Learning-Derived Subtypes of Autism Reveal Distinct Genetic Contributions from Common and Rare Variants
items.title_zh: 机器学习衍生的自闭症亚型揭示常见与罕见变异的独特遗传贡献
items.abstract_en: Background: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is characterized by substantial heterogeneity in core symptom severity and co-occurring conditions, complicating efforts to understand its genetic basis. Most genetic studies rely on binary case-control ASD definitions, which may obscure clinically meaningful variation and distinct genetic contributions across the autism spectrum. Methods: We constructed machine learning (ML)-based categorical ASD subtypes and corresponding continuous ASD subtype scores using 14 key clinical symptom measures with adjustment of sex and age among 6,355 autistic children in the Simons Foundation Powering Autism Research for Knowledge (SPARK) cohort by Discriminative Dimensionality Reduction via learning a Tree (DDRTree). We then replicated and validated these subtypes and scores among 2,717 autistic children in the Simons Simplex Collection (SSC) using a modified k-nearest-neighbor (k-NN) approach. In SPARK and SSC, we further clinically validated the framework by examining associations of subtype classifications and scores with support needs, service utilization and medication use by regression models with adjustment for sex, age, genetic ancestry and socioeconomic factors. We further assessed SNP-based heritability, cell-type-specific heritability enrichment, polygenic scores (PGS) for psychiatric and cognitive traits, as well as rare copy-number variant (CNV) and de novo variant (DNV) burdens across the ML-derived ASD subtype scores adjusting for sex, age and genetic ancestry. Results: We identified three clinically distinct ASD subtypes in SPARK varying in the types of supports utilized: a high-support-needs (HSN) subtype characterized by broad developmental and functional impairments and very substantial support needs (OR = 1.63, P = 3.71 x 10-98); an emotional-behavioral-support-needs (EBSN) subtype marked by severe repetitive behaviors, elevated psychiatric comorbidity; and a low-support-needs (LSN) subtype with milder symptoms and relatively lower overall support needs. The three groups were associated with differential patterns in the specific types of treatments that were most common for them, from higher intensity to lower intensity. Projected ASD subtypes and scores in SSC recapitulated the phenotypic and medication-use patterns observed in SPARK. SNP-based heritability was highest for the EBSN score (h2g = 0.224, SE = 0.051) followed by the HSN (h2g = 0.167, SE = 0.049) and LSN score (h2g = 0.064, SE = 0.044), with suggestive cell-type-specific heritability enrichments in fetal endodermal cells and adult motor neurons for EBSN score and fetal excitatory neurons and astrocytes for HSN score (both P < 0.05). PGS of ADHD and major depressive disorder were consistently associated with higher EBSN scores in both SPARK and SSC. Higher DNV and rare CNV burden were associated with higher HSN score in SPARK, and higher rare CNV burden was associated with higher EBSN score in SSC (P < 0.05). Conclusions: Our ML-based transferable ASD subtype framework captured clinically and genetically meaningful dimensions of ASD heterogeneity, warranting further validation in larger cohorts. Keywords: Autism spectrum disorder, phenotypic heterogeneity, subtypes, machine learning, genetic burden
items.abstract_zh: 背景：自闭症谱系障碍（ASD）在核心症状严重程度与共病上高度异质，这使解析其遗传基础变得困难。多数遗传研究采用二分类病例-对照定义，可能掩盖临床上有意义的差异以及谱系内不同的遗传贡献。方法：我们在SPARK队列6,355名自闭症儿童中，基于14项关键临床症状测量（校正性别与年龄），用DDRTree（通过树结构学习的判别性降维）构建机器学习（ML）分类亚型及对应的连续亚型评分；随后在Simons Simplex Collection（SSC）的2,717名自闭症儿童中，用改良k近邻（k-NN）方法复现并验证这些亚型与评分。在两个队列中，我们进一步用回归模型（校正性别、年龄、遗传祖先与社会经济因素）检验亚型分类和评分与支持需求、服务使用和用药的关联；并评估各亚型评分下的SNP遗传力、细胞类型特异遗传力富集、精神与认知性状的多基因评分（PGS），以及罕见拷贝数变异（CNV）和新发变异（DNV）负荷。结果：在SPARK中识别出三种临床可区分的ASD亚型，其使用的支持服务类型不同；其中高支持需求（HSN）亚型以广泛的发育与功能损害和极高的支持需求为特征（OR=1.63）。
items.highlight_zh: 用机器学习把自闭症分为三个临床亚型，常见与罕见变异贡献各异
items.digest_zh:
1. 研究了什么问题：自闭症谱系障碍（ASD）个体差异极大——症状轻重、共病、所需支持都不同。但遗传研究长期把ASD当成“有病/没病”的二元标签，这种粗分类可能把真正有生物学意义的差异抹平了，导致遗传信号难以解析。
2. 用了什么方法：作者在SPARK队列的6,355名自闭症儿童中，取14项核心临床症状测量，校正性别和年龄后，用DDRTree（一种通过树结构做判别性降维的方法）无监督地划出亚型，并给出每个孩子的连续亚型评分。随后在独立队列SSC的2,717名儿童中，用改良的k近邻方法把新个体映射到这些亚型上做复现验证。他们还在两个队列中用回归模型检验亚型与支持需求、服务使用、用药的关系，并计算SNP遗传力、细胞类型特异遗传力富集、精神与认知相关性状的多基因评分（PGS），以及罕见CNV和新发变异（DNV）负荷在各亚型评分上的差异。
3. 有什么结果：在SPARK中识别出三种临床上可区分的亚型，区别主要体现在所需支持服务的类型上。其中“高支持需求”（HSN）亚型表现为广泛的发育与功能损害、支持需求极高（OR=1.63）。遗传分析显示，不同亚型背后常见变异（如PGS、SNP遗传力）与罕见变异（CNV、DNV）的贡献并不相同，说明ASD的遗传结构在不同临床表现下存在分化。
4. 为何重要：这项工作把ASD从单一标签拆解为可量化的临床-遗传亚型维度，为解释“同样诊断、遗传基础却不同”提供了框架。对临床而言，亚型评分有望帮助预判支持需求；对遗传研究而言，提示按亚型分组分析可能提升发现致病因素的能力。

items.title_en: Shared clones make random cell halves look reproducible in pooled screens
items.abstract_en: Single-cell perturbation screens are used to train and evaluate models that predict perturbation effects, and model scores are judged against how reproducible the measured effects are. Reproducibility is usually judged by splitting each perturbation's cells into two random halves. This assumes that the halves are independent replicates. In pooled screens such as Perturb-seq, however, the cells carrying a guide RNA descend from a limited number of transduced cells, so two random halves contain the same clones: pseudoreplication whose unit is not marked in the data. Using perturbations that should have no effect as controls, we compared random halves with independent replicates from separate transductions, and tested directly with halves that differ only in their clones. In a genome-scale screen of primary T cells, null perturbations agreed between random halves almost always and between independent replicates only half the time, the rate expected from noise alone; measuring more cells did not remove this agreement. Splitting the cells into halves that share no clone, by the T-cell receptor constant region or by a clone barcode, largely removed the excess agreement. Its size equals the share of expression differences set by clones divided by the effective number of clones per perturbation; across 16 screens it was largest in T cells transferred into mice and in a genome-scale primary T-cell screen, one to two orders of magnitude smaller in cell lines, and smallest in non-dividing neurons. Shared clones inflate benchmark ceilings and reliability labels, and when a model's input and its scoring answer come from one transduction, published models that predict perturbation effects in a new cell state appear better than a baseline that ignores the perturbation; against cells from another transduction, most fall below it. Reproducibility should be judged across separate transductions.

items.title_en: ZENO: Nonlinear filtering with Zakai Equation Neural Operators
items.abstract_en: State inference and parameter learning for nonlinear filters is a core computation for scientific machine learning with varied applications in engineering and neuroscience. The unnormalized filtering distribution is governed by the Zakai equation, a stochastic partial differential equation (SPDE) that combines the forward Kolmogorov operator (known as the Fokker-Planck equation) with observed likelihood updates. Although solving these high-dimensional SPDEs is often impossible analytically and intractable numerically, advances in operator learning and physics-informed machine learning have made it feasible. Harnessing these advances, we introduce the Zakai Equation Neural Operator (ZENO), a model that optimizes a neural operator against a Zakai Equation based physics-informed loss to approximate the exact unnormalized filtering distribution for latent stochastic dynamical systems. We use this ZENO-inferred posterior distribution in an expectation-maximization (EM) framework to perform parameter learning and state inference. We demonstrate ZENO's ability to accurately infer the posterior distribution and learn its corresponding SDE parameters in three simulated stochastic dynamical systems (Double-Well bistable system, Van Der Pol (VDP) oscillator, and Lorenz system) and compare its performance against established methods for latent SDE inference and learning. We show that ZENO recovers previously observed limit cycles representing forward and backward locomotion from a whole-brain imaging dataset of immobilized \textit{C. elegans} nematodes. ZENO is a novel approach to the problem of nonlinear filtering and dynamical inference through the lens of partial differential equations and operator theory.

items.title_en: Computational De Novo Design of Miniprotein Candidate Neutralizers Targeting the IL-23 Cytokine Subunit p19
items.abstract_en: Interleukin-23 (IL-23) drives T-helper-17 inflammation underlying inflammatory bowel disease and psoriasis; anti-p19 antibodies are clinically effective but large, costly, and injectable. De novo miniproteins are an attractive alternative, yet published designs target the IL-23 receptor; the IL-23 cytokine itself has not been addressed. A further obstacle is that the standard confidence score (ipTM) tracks construct length rather than interface quality. We computationally design miniprotein binders against the IL-23R-binding face of p19 (PDB 3DUH) and score every design with ipSAE, a length-robust interface metric derived from AlphaFold-initial-guess predicted aligned error. A conventional RFdiffusion/ProteinMPNN/ColabFold pipeline yields no reliable predicted interface across 972 designs (best ipSAE 0.30), and a scoring artifact, in which single-sequence ColabFold under-rates binder pLDDT by approximately 56 points, explains an earlier misleading "binders do not fold" signal. An interface-optimized hallucination method (BindCraft), scored identically, yields 42 of 50 designs above ipSAE 0.60 (best 0.804). An AlphaFold-independent geometric check reproduces the conventional failure: no top-ranked conventional design reaches the buried area or interface hydrogen-bond count of the weakest lead. Five all-alpha-helical leads (72-104 residues) collectively engage all six targeted hotspots; two dock within the intact p40/p19 heterodimer and all show favorable Rosetta energetics. A p40-alone counter-screen returns ipSAE 0.00 for all five, indicating no spurious p40 interface. To our knowledge, these are the first computationally proposed de novo miniprotein candidates designed to occlude the IL-23R-binding face of IL-23 p19. All results require experimental validation.

items.title_en: Video-rate quantitative phase and polarimetric imaging (QP2I) for label-free imaging of contracting muscle cells
items.title_zh: 用于收缩肌细胞无标记成像的视频速率定量相位与偏振成像（QP2I）
items.abstract_en: Quantitative phase imaging (QPI) has become a standard approach for label-free microscopy of transparent specimens, mapping the optical path length. However, the isotropic phase is blind to the molecular order underlying optical anisotropy. Implementations that also add quantitative contrast to birefringence, rely on multi-frame illumination or polarization-state scanning, or on dedicated interferometric hardware, that trade away acquisition speed or the simplicity of a standard microscope. We present Quantitative Phase and Polarimetric Imaging (QP2I), a computational imaging framework that converts a standard differential interference contrast (DIC) microscope with a polarization camera into a single-shot, video-rate, dual-contrast imaging system. We developed a new globally regularized phase reconstruction that eliminates artifacts of prior DIC-to-QPI approaches, providing quantitative phase information and used per-pixel Stokes-based reconstruction to obtain quantitative anisotropic retardance. We validate the approach across simulations, static reference targets, fixed muscle tissue and living dynamically moving cells. Thereby, QP2I enables to study contractile dynamics in live cardiomyocytes all-optically and label-free. It provides both structural and functional readouts at frame rates that are sufficient to temporally resolve fast cardiomyocyte contractions. While conventional fluorescent labels bleach out over time, perturb physiology, and preclude long-term monitoring, QP2I provides similar established structural readouts, such as frame-by-frame sarcomere length, as well as previously inaccessible measurements, like quantitative analysis of retardance changes during muscle contraction, as a direct optical signature of muscle photoelasticity. QP2I thus enables long-term, label-free interrogation of dynamic cellular processes at quantitative contrast.

items.title_en: What Transfers Across Protein Pockets? Experience Reuse in Molecular Optimization for Agentic Structure-Based Drug Design
items.title_zh: 什么可跨蛋白质口袋迁移？面向智能体式基于结构药物设计的分子优化中的经验复用
items.abstract_en: LLM agents optimize a ligand in a protein pocket by editing it step by step and docking each edit. Recent agents first spend extra dockings probing the complex with controlled edits; guidance induced from these probes is reported to help more than the chemical knowledge the model already carries. The probes are then discarded with the instance that produced them, so the obvious next step is to keep them in an experience base, letting a new pocket inherit what earlier ones already paid for. Such a base is read through a \emph{key}: the record properties under which past edits are pooled and a new one is looked up. Using the full log of one such run over the CrossDocked2020 test-set pockets, we ask whether its keys recur on a pocket the base has never seen and still separate improving from worsening edits. \crchange{Using} the contacts at the site being edited, the action, and the round as \crchange{a} key, the base separates them sharply. Within our analysis, this separation is largely explained by how much the edit changed the molecule's size, the action, and the round, none of which describes the target. That is not because the target is irrelevant: naming it outright separates them several times more sharply. For a pocket absent from the base, transfer must rely on a description rather than its identity. Among the exact-match descriptions we evaluate, the more specific ones rarely recur, whereas the coarser ones provide little separation; the signals that do transfer primarily describe the edit and the molecule it produced rather than the target. Under the representations and lookup scheme studied here, an experience base may be more useful for prioritizing an agent's own proposals for docking than for directly prescribing what to build.

items.title_en: Estimation of the Cyclopean Eye from Binocular Free Visual Explorations
items.abstract_en: Binocular video-oculography records separate signals for each eye, yet human visual processing and oculomotor control operate relative to a single, virtual cyclopean eye. This study addresses the estimation of the cyclopean eye during binocular free visual exploration, a target-free paradigm widely used for the screening of neurological disorders. Using eye-tracking data collected at 1 kHz from 113 participants across three cohorts (patients with Parkinson's Disease, age-matched healthy controls, and young controls), we compare two different methods: one based on an Independent Component Analysis and another based on Factor Analysis. The extracted cyclopean signals were evaluated on their ability to preserve clinically critical fixation and saccadic events using both velocity-threshold and pixel-dispersion event detectors, and were validated against references via Dynamic Time Warping. Results suggest that the technique based on Factor Analysis guarantees full identifiability across all subjects and achieves low alignment errors, performing comparably to the traditional Version Signal (point-wise mean) while dynamically adapting to inter-eye asymmetry. Furthermore, the second factor in this technique was empirically null across all fitted models, confirming that a single latent factor fully accounts for the shared binocular gaze dynamics. These findings establish Factor Analysis as an identifiable framework for estimating the cyclopean eye in target-free visual exploration protocols.

items.title_en: From Heterogeneity to Function: Enhanced Modular Dynamic Range in Hierarchical Brain Networks
items.abstract_en: Hierarchical and modular organization defines brain architecture, yet how it supports flexible computation and functional specialization remains unclear. Although dynamic range is a hallmark of efficient information processing, its distribution across modules and hierarchical levels remains largely unexplored. Here, we show that hierarchical-modular networks naturally generate heterogeneous modular dynamics and firing rates, extending regimes of critical-like dynamics with enhanced intrinsic timescales, reflecting critical slowing down, and diverse scaling exponents without fine-tuning near criticality. Intrinsic timescales increase across hierarchical levels, while their dispersion within levels emerges only when connectivity profiles and firing rates are heterogeneous. We introduce modular dynamic range to quantify how individual modules respond to external inputs and show that heterogeneity enhances both global and module-specific sensitivity, with modular intrinsic timescales increasing with dynamic range. Local stimulation reduces dynamic range in homogeneous networks but enhances it in heterogeneous networks relative to global stimulation. Moreover, selectively stimulating intermediate hierarchical levels maximizes both global and modular dynamic range, revealing a principle of functional specialization. In heterogeneous networks, modular dynamic range is more variable and increases even in unstimulated modules, demonstrating distributed computational benefits beyond directly stimulated regions. Together, these findings establish heterogeneity as a mechanism through which hierarchical-modular networks sustain critical-like dynamics, generate hierarchical timescales, and distribute computational sensitivity, providing a basis for functional specialization without fine-tuning to criticality.

items.title_en: Maximal Orbital Entanglement from Non-Interacting Fermions
items.title_zh: 无相互作用费米子携带的最大轨道纠缠
items.abstract_en: Orbital rotations are used in quantum many-body physics and chemistry to reduce the complexity of quantum states by compressing their correlation into a small set of relevant orbitals. In striking contrast, quantum information processing strives for the opposite: orbitals that maximize entanglement as a resource. Motivated by this, we prove that Slater determinants of $N$ fermions on a lattice of $d_A + d_B = d$ sites, although free of particle correlation, can carry up to $\min\{d_A, d_B, N, d-N\}$ ebits of orbital entanglement. Given enough particles and holes, this equals the maximum over all fermionic states. For arbitrary free states, we derive the maximal orbital total correlation in closed form for all bipartitions, the finest partition, and all partitions of up to five sites, using new majorization relations for Hermitian matrices. Taken together, these results turn mean-field states, the starting point of most many-body methods in physics and chemistry, into a viable resource for quantum information processing.
items.abstract_zh: 轨道旋转在量子多体物理与化学中被用来把量子态的关联压缩到少数几个相关轨道上，从而降低复杂性；量子信息处理的目标恰恰相反——要寻找使纠缠最大化的轨道。受此启发，我们证明：在 d_A + d_B = d 个格点上，N 个费米子的 Slater 行列式虽然不含粒子关联，却能携带最多 min{d_A, d_B, N, d-N} ebit 的轨道纠缠；当粒子数与空穴数足够时，这一上界等于所有费米态的最大值。对于任意自由态，我们借助新的厄米矩阵 majorization 关系，给出了所有二分、最细划分以及至多五个格点的全部分划下最大轨道总关联的闭式解。这些结果把物理与化学中多数多体方法的起点——平均场态——变成了量子信息处理可用的资源。
items.highlight_zh: 无关联的 Slater 行列式即可承载最大轨道纠缠
items.digest_zh:
【研究了什么问题】在量子化学和量子多体物理里，人们常做“轨道旋转”，把复杂的关联压缩进少数几个轨道，方便计算；而量子信息处理却希望轨道之间尽可能纠缠，把纠缠当作资源。这两种诉求看似矛盾，作者追问：最“简单”的态，也就是无相互作用的费米子所构成的 Slater 行列式（平均场态），究竟能承载多少轨道纠缠？

【用了什么方法】这是一项理论工作：把格点分成 A、B 两部分，考察费米子在各轨道上的占据方式所诱导的纠缠，并用厄米矩阵的 majorization（优超）关系推导上界与闭式表达式。

【有什么结果】证明了 N 个费米子在 d_A+d_B=d 个格点上，Slater 行列式最多能提供 min{d_A, d_B, N, d-N} ebit 的轨道纠缠；在粒子与空穴都足够多时，这正好是所有费米态所能达到的最大值，也就是说自由态此前未被发现也能达到“满格”纠缠。进一步，作者给出了任意自由态在各类二分割、最细分割以及至多五个格点全部分割下的最大轨道总关联的闭式解。

【为何重要】平均场态是所有多体方法的起点，计算极其容易制备与操控。若它们本身就天然携带最大纠缠，那么量子信息处理可以直接借用成熟的平均场工具箱，而无需构造高度复杂的关联态，这为量子资源理论开辟了一条低成本路径。

items.title_en: Ideal interaction dynamics of defects and background fields in condensed matter
items.title_zh: 凝聚态中缺陷与背景场的理想相互作用动力学
items.abstract_en: While defect dynamics in condensed matter systems is widely studied and several methods are available to track the defect position over time, the formulation of dynamical models for the coupled evolution of both defect and background field quantities seems to be more challenging. Yet, the overall behavior of a system containing moving defects is strongly influenced by this defect-field interaction. Here, we propose a modeling framework for the conservative coupled evolution of the defect density and the background fields upon focusing on two relevant cases of study: the Gross-Pitaevskii theory of quantum fluids and the Ericksen-Leslie model of nematic liquid crystals. To achieve the coupled evolution, we combine the Euler-Poincaré variational setting of continuum dynamics with the gauge theory of topological defects. While the latter allows us to overcome certain ambiguities in definition of the defect density, the Euler-Poincaré method provides a unified modeling approach in the absence of defect reconnection.
items.abstract_zh: 凝聚态系统中缺陷动力学已被广泛研究，并有多种方法可追踪缺陷位置随时间的变化，但为缺陷与背景场二者的耦合演化建立动力学模型仍较困难；而含有运动缺陷的系统的整体行为，恰恰强烈受这种缺陷—场相互作用影响。本文提出一个建模框架，用于缺陷密度与背景场的保守耦合演化，聚焦两个代表性案例：量子流体的 Gross-Pitaevskii 理论与向列液晶的 Ericksen-Leslie 模型。为实现耦合演化，我们将连续介质动力学的 Euler-Poincaré 变分框架与拓扑缺陷的规范理论相结合：后者可消除缺陷密度定义中的某些歧义，前者则在无缺陷重联的情形下提供统一的建模途径。
items.highlight_zh: 用 Euler-Poincaré 变分加规范理论统一刻画缺陷与场耦合演化
items.digest_zh:
【研究了什么问题】在液体、液晶、超流等凝聚态系统中，“缺陷”（如涡旋、向错线）会移动，它们周围的背景场也随之改变，反过来又推动缺陷运动。追踪单个缺陷位置的方法已有不少，但要把“缺陷密度”和“背景场”放在同一套方程里耦合地演化，一直缺乏统一、严谨的动力学模型。

【用了什么方法】作者把两类数学工具拼在一起：一是连续介质力学的 Euler-Poincaré 变分框架，它从作用量原理出发，能保证方程具有变分结构与守恒性；二是拓扑缺陷的规范理论，它把缺陷当作规范场的奇异性来处理，从而避开“缺陷密度到底怎么定义”这一长期存在的模糊之处。文中具体落地到两个经典模型：描述量子流体的 Gross-Pitaevskii 方程，和描述向列液晶的 Ericksen-Leslie 方程。

【有什么结果】建立了一个“保守”（无耗散）的耦合演化框架，让缺陷密度与背景场可以自洽地一起演化；并说明该框架在缺陷不发生重联的情形下是统一的、可操作的。

【为何重要】许多材料的宏观行为由运动缺陷主导，例如超流中的涡旋、液晶中的拓扑缺陷。有了这样的耦合动力学，就能更可靠地预测和模拟含缺陷材料的演化，也为后续把耗散、缺陷重联等更复杂效应纳入进来提供了严谨的出发点。

items.title_en: Distributed Quantum-Centric Supercomputing with Multi-Layered Generative Learning for Intermolecular Interactions
items.title_zh: 面向分子间相互作用的分布式量子中心超算与多层生成学习
items.abstract_en: Quantum-centric supercomputing (QCSC) approaches, such as sample-based quantum diagonalization (SQD), combine quantum processors with high-performance computers (HPC), offering a promising route toward solving challenging electronic structure problems. However, implementation of QCSC approaches to large active space calculations is constrained by the associated number of qubits, deep quantum circuits, sampling cost, and large-scale Hamiltonian diagonalization. To overcome these limitations, we introduce a distributed QCSC framework that decomposes complex molecular problems into parallel sub-problems requiring fewer qubits, shallower circuits, and reduced shot budgets. A physically motivated, two-step aggregation scheme then reconstructs the global solution: first, a computational bit assignment strategy optimizes a cost function to appropriately map local bit indices to global ones, yielding a mapped tensor product state (MTPS); second, an inter-fragment correlation recovery module restores missing cross-fragment interactions. Herein, we employ a multi-layered generative machine learning architecture, starting with utilizing the recently proposed physics-informed generative SQD (PIGen-SQD) as a distributed QCSC solver, followed by a secondary generative module to model configuration distributions and identify dominant sectors of the global Hilbert space. For water and formamide dimers, our method achieves up to $95\%$ reduction in the diagonalization dimension while enhancing energy accuracy by an order of magnitude over conventional SQD. Furthermore, application to the water hexamer ($\mathrm{(H_2O)_6}$) cage successfully decomposes a 120-qubit problem into six 20-qubit monomeric subsystems, and stitches the monomers under a dimeric approximation, demonstrating excellent agreement with the reference classical methods.
items.abstract_zh: 以采样量子对角化（SQD）为代表的量子中心超算（QCSC）方法，将量子处理器与高性能计算（HPC）结合，为求解困难的电子结构问题提供了有前景的途径。但将其用于大活性空间计算时，受制于量子比特数、电路深度、采样成本以及大规模哈密顿量对角化。为突破这些限制，我们提出分布式 QCSC 框架，把复杂分子问题分解为并行的子问题，从而需要更少量子比特、更浅电路和更小采样预算；随后用物理启发的两步聚合方案重建全局解：先用计算比特分配策略优化代价函数，把局部比特索引映射到全局，得到映射张量积态（MTPS）；再用碎片间关联恢复模块补回缺失的跨碎片相互作用。其中我们采用多层生成式机器学习架构：先以物理启发的生成式 SQD（PIGen-SQD）作为分布式 QCSC 求解器，再用第二个生成模块建模构型分布、识别全局希尔伯特空间的主导扇区。对水二聚体与甲酰胺二聚体，本方法使对角化维度最多降低 95%，能量精度比常规 SQD 提升一个数量级；应用于水六聚体（(H2O)6）笼状结构时，成功把一个 120 量子比特的问题分解为六个 20 量子比特的单体子系统，并在二聚体近似下拼接单体。
items.highlight_zh: 把大分子问题拆成小量子比特子问题，精度反升一个数量级
items.digest_zh:
【研究了什么问题】量子中心超算（QCSC）把量子处理器与经典高性能计算结合，其中 SQD 一类方法先让量子计算机采样、再由经典计算机做对角化。但分子一大、活性空间一大，就需要更多量子比特、更深的电路、更多的采样次数，以及规模大到难以承受的哈密顿量对角化，导致这类方法“上不了大分子”。

【用了什么方法】作者提出“分布式”思路：把一个复杂分子拆成若干碎片子问题并行求解，每块只需要少量量子比特和浅电路。难点在于如何把碎片的解拼回全局解，于是设计了两步聚合：第一步是“计算比特分配”，通过优化一个代价函数决定局部比特索引如何对应到全局索引，得到映射张量积态 MTPS；第二步是“碎片间关联恢复”，把拆分时丢掉的跨碎片相互作用补回来。整个流程由多层生成式机器学习架构驱动：底层用他们此前的 PIGen-SQD 作为分布式求解器，上层再加一个生成模块，学习构型分布、找出全局希尔伯特空间中真正占主导的扇区。

【有什么结果】在水二聚体和甲酰胺二聚体上，对角化维度最多减少 95%，同时能量精度比传统 SQD 提高约一个数量级；在水六聚体笼状结构上，把 120 量子比特的问题拆成六个 20 量子比特的单体子系统，并在二聚体近似下成功拼接。

【为何重要】它说明“分而治之”可以在不牺牲精度的前提下大幅降低量子资源需求，为近期含噪声量子设备处理真实分子间相互作用（如氢键网络、溶剂化）提供了可扩展的路线。

items.title_en: Low-frustration block encodings by patch routing
items.title_zh: 通过 patch routing 的低阻挫块编码
items.abstract_en: Block-encoding has emerged as a core primitive in many quantum algorithms, including quantum simulation. In this work, we design efficient and extensible methods for generating low-frustration block encodings of frustrated lattice Hamiltonians built from repeated local interaction patches through a technique we call "patch routing". We construct block encodings for a full Hamiltonian by first block-encoding a small local patch and then using a SWAP-style routing network to coherently apply the local patch encoding across the lattice. The expensive, local block-encoding cost is paid only once per query and is independent of lattice size, whereas the comparatively inexpensive routing network grows linearly with the lattice size, dominating at large sizes. Our method allows for a hierarchical structure in which larger patches can be block-encoded with small normalization factors, albeit at a higher (local, non-extensive) block-encoding cost, thereby reducing overall query complexity in an algorithm. We exploit symmetries and algebraic structures in local interactions to construct efficient block encodings, and we apply these techniques to the Heisenberg, Fermi-Hubbard, and honeycomb spin-liquid models. For a $120\times 120$ square-lattice $J_1$-$J_2$ Heisenberg model near maximal frustration ($J_2/J_1=0.4-0.6$), our methods result in a $15-17\times$ reduction in the leading $T$ cost per qubitized-QPE run (ignoring initial state preparation and overlap) relative to prior state-of-the-art Pauli LCU constructions. Corresponding reductions are approximately $3\times$ for the $120\times120$ Fermi-Hubbard model at half-filling. For time evolution of the honeycomb spin-liquid model on $120\times120$ unit cells, the leading cost is reduced by $5\times$. Our framework provides a systematic way forward for larger and more accurate fault-tolerant simulations of real-world quantum systems.

items.title_en: Certain Quantum States Already Require Quantum Time Evolution
items.title_zh: 某些量子态已经需要量子时间演化
items.abstract_en: Model-independent tests of quantum theory, such as Bell inequality violations, focus on static properties of the theory and do not rely on its dynamical aspects. Hence, this core part of quantum theory remains largely untested in a model-independent way. We show that the structure of quantum time evolution can be examined by testing the consistency between the state space and the dynamical laws. Considering a class of generalized phase-space theories, we find that certain quantum states can only be part of a theory if the time evolution is quantum: their evolution in anharmonic potentials would otherwise result in unphysical, negative marginal distributions. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the existence of the first excited state of a quantum harmonic oscillator is already sufficient to single out the Moyal bracket (quantum dynamics) to leading order in $\hbar^2$. We outline how theory-independent Wigner tomography of this state can be used to empirically exclude nonquantum dynamical theories.

items.title_en: Generating entanglement in quantum matter with pathway-entangled photons via resonant inelastic X-ray scattering
items.title_zh: 通过共振非弹性 X 射线散射利用路径纠缠光子在量子物质中产生纠缠
items.abstract_en: Resonant inelastic X-ray scattering (RIXS) is conventionally used to probe elementary excitations and correlations in quantum materials. Here, we propose an interferometric RIXS protocol that instead creates entanglement between spatially separated regions of a solid-state material. An incident X-ray photon is coherently split by a beam splitter into two arms illuminating opposite ends of a sample. Recombining the scattered photons at a second beam splitter and detecting an energy-selected photon then projects the material into a coherent superposition of excitations at the two ends. This protocol is the X-ray, solid-state analogue of the Duan-Lukin-Cirac-Zoller (DLCZ) heralding scheme. Using a Kramers-Heisenberg formalism with quantized photon modes, we show that orthogonal and degenerate end excitations yield maximally entangled states. We illustrate this mechanism in three models: (1) two decoupled sites yield a heralded Bell state. (2) An open tight-binding chain exhibits reflection-parity-dependent interference, providing a benchmark for the interferometer's coherence. (3) A spin-1 Haldane (AKLT) chain yields an entangled pair of fractionalized edge spins. We also discuss practical considerations and challenges for realizing the protocol in X-ray experiments.

items.title_en: Scaling the Wavelength to Optimize Ultrafast Laser Processing of Bandgap Materials
items.title_zh: 通过波长缩放优化带隙材料的超快激光加工
items.abstract_en: The spectral characteristics of ultrashort laser pulses offer unique possibilities to control interactions in space and time as well as the subsequent material responses. In particular, selecting the wavelength predefines the fundamental mechanisms governing laser-matter interaction, and thus, how energy is deposited. This Chapter provides an overview on how the essential physical effects in ultrafast laser-matter interaction scale with the wavelength, and the consequences for bandgap material processing applications. First, we recall the main spectral properties of bandgap materials and discuss the important question of the expected processing resolutions depending on wavelength. Then, recent studies on the impact of the wavelength in ultrafast laser-dielectric interaction are presented. Finally, we present how the latest developments in infrared ultrafast laser sources can be advantageously utilized to internally process narrow-gap materials despite challenges related to increased nonlinearities.

items.title_en: One-sided-DIQKD using any pure bipartite entangled state secure against all attacks
items.title_zh: 使用任意纯二分纠缠态且可抵御所有攻击的单边 DIQKD
items.abstract_en: Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) allows spatially separated parties to establish a secret key among themselves based on quantum principles. While QKD systems are being deployed worldwide, their reliance on trusted measurements makes them vulnerable. Moreover, existing protocols have largely focussed on the qubit cases, and rely on the maximally entangled state, a costly resource to generate. Here, we consider the one-sided-device-independent (1SDI) QKD protocols, where one of the measurement devices is trusted while the other is untrusted. The resource in this scenario is quantum steering, an asymmetric form of quantum nonlocality. This is inspired by a real-world scenario, where the trusted party can be considered to be a bank, or any large organisation that has sufficient resources to protect its systems and validate them, while the users are vulnerable to attacks. We then demonstrate that a secure key can be obtained using any pure bipartite entangled state in this setup. Considering realistic detectors and sources based on current technology, we demonstrate that even states that are almost separable can be used to extract a secure key. Moreover, for every pure entangled bipartite state, we find the critical detection efficiencies and visibility to obtain a secure key.

items.title_en: Nonclassicality from Incomplete Fock-State Statistics
items.title_zh: 不完全福克态统计中的非经典性
items.abstract_en: Nonclassicality in bosonic systems can be certified directly from occupation probabilities without full state reconstruction. To complete a library of such criteria we introduce a numerical framework that constructs optimal linear nonclassicality witnesses from arbitrary subsets of measured occupation probabilities by solving a semi-infinite linear program. The method contains known analytical criteria as special cases while generally detecting substantially larger nonclassical regions. We provide an open-source implementation of the numerical optimization together with the analytical criteria discussed here, enabling direct application of the framework to measured occupation statistics across bosonic platforms. As a case study, we apply it to the resonant Jaynes--Cummings model with thermal states and reveal nonclassicality at short interaction times and close to thermal balance, where detection of nonclassicality is otherwise challenging.

items.title_en: Polarization-encoded photon statistics for counting dipole emitters
items.title_zh: 用于计数偶极发射体的偏振编码光子统计
items.abstract_en: Counting the emitters within a diffraction-limited region is a prerequisite for localizing overlapping molecules. Under pulsed excitation, each molecule emits at most one photon per pulse, so photon-number-resolved detection can count emitters without resolving them. But the required number of pulses grows steeply with the emitter number. Here we show that polarization, conventionally used to measure the orientations of dipole emitters, also carries information on their number. Because mean polarization-resolved signals are unchanged when every emitter is replaced by multiple dimmer copies, this information resides in the photon statistics within each pulse, which polarization reshapes in two ways. Linearly polarized excitation at three angles increases the sub-Poissonian deficit of the photon count by a factor of 1.5 for any emitter orientation, and detection in four polarization channels reveals the emitter number through how the photons of multiphoton pulses are distributed among the channels. Maximum-likelihood simulations for two to five emitters of unknown orientations and brightnesses show that three-angle excitation reduces the required number of pulses by about 2.3-fold, close to the predicted $1.5^2=2.25$, and that adding four-channel detection raises the reduction to as much as 4.8-fold. These gains require only polarization optics added to photon-number-resolved detection.

items.title_en: Fermion Scattering on Quantum Computers
items.title_zh: 量子计算机上的费米子散射
items.abstract_en: Resonant scattering links particle interactions to the formation and decay of unstable excitations. We develop a hybrid quantum-computing framework to study these dynamics through fermion--antifermion collisions. Our formulation of $(1+1)$-dimensional Yukawa theory encodes fermions in qubits and the scalar field in qumodes. We identify the operations needed for a photonic implementation and benchmark the dynamics with tensor-network simulations. Near resonance, we resolve the build-up of a localised scalar excitation and the subsequent partial return of energy to the fermions. Enhanced entanglement accompanies this exchange. Time-dependent correlator measurements reproduce the analytically predicted decay rate to a few percent precision, with energy scans exhibiting a resonance peak consistent with packet-averaged Breit--Wigner behaviour. These results establish a concrete scattering benchmark for hybrid quantum computers and demonstrate how local real-time observables can probe particle-resonance dynamics.

items.title_en: Hardware-Friendly Estimation of LCU-Based Expectation Values via Quantum-to-Classical Workload Shifting
items.title_zh: 通过量子到经典工作负载转移的硬件友好型基于LCU的期望值估计
items.abstract_en: Estimating the expectation value of an observable $O$ for a quantum state evolved under a general, possibly non-unitary, operator $A$ is a fundamental task in quantum simulation, chemistry, and variational algorithms. Existing linear-combination-of-unitaries (LCU) approaches implement $A$ on hardware, requiring ancilla qubits, controlled unitaries and, in randomized variants, fresh circuit executions for every Monte Carlo sample. These costs are prohibitive on NISQ and early fault-tolerant devices. We propose HERMES (Hardware-Efficient Reusable Measurements for Estimating LCU-based expectation valueS), which moves the processing of $A$ entirely to the classical domain. Expanding $A$ and $O$ in the Pauli basis and sampling pairs of Pauli terms classically, HERMES rewrites $μ= \mathrm{Tr}(OAρA^{\dagger})/\mathrm{Tr}(AρA^{\dagger})$ as a ratio of weighted sums of Pauli expectation values on the unmodified state $ρ$, with no ancillas, controlled unitaries, or quantum implementation of $A$. A two-level measurement reduction scheme (Pauli deduplication and commuting-group partitioning) bounds the number of distinct measurement settings independently of the sample count, unlike randomized LCU methods whose circuit executions grow linearly with it. On ground-state energy estimation of $\mathrm{H}_2$ and $\mathrm{LiH}$ via imaginary-time evolution, HERMES matches or beats Pauli single-ancilla LCU baseline using shallow circuits with no two-qubit gates beyond state preparation under qubit-wise commuting grouping. It is also more robust to noise and completes a noisy $\mathrm{LiH}$ simulation infeasible for the baseline, at the cost of classical overhead growing with the number of Pauli terms in $A$.

items.title_en: Modular optical fault-tolerant quantum computation via an interface between verified resources and online logical operations
items.title_zh: 经由已验证资源与在线逻辑操作之间接口的模块化光学容错量子计算
items.abstract_en: We introduce a factory--processor interface architecture for modular optical fault-tolerant quantum computation that separates code-dependent encoded-resource preparation from reusable online logical processing on a common Gaussian optical processor. Beyond encoded resources, the interface specifies logical outputs, code-to-mode mapping, measurement roles, frame updates, verification records, and resource-injection boundaries. As a concrete realization, we combine an offline verified Bell-resource factory based on a recursively concatenated $C_4$ code with physical Gottesman--Kitaev--Preskill (GKP) qubits with an online time-domain measurement-based quantum computation (MBQC) processor. Under the specified additive-displacement-noise model and fixed postselection policy, simulations support the finite-level logical Bell-error ordering $P_5<P_4<P_3<P_2$ at 12.25 dB of effective GKP displacement-noise quality, both with and without the prescribed additional post-injection displacement noise. At 15.6 dB and $L=2$, a separate fixed-sample evaluation gives one-sided 95$\%$ Clopper--Pearson upper bounds below $10^{-5}$ for both conditions under the binomial model. The interface supports address-tracked injection, transversal CNOT and logical Bell-measurement constructions, and logical SWAP and Hadamard constructions with tracked code permutations. Given advance resource preparation and sufficient routing parallelism, increasing the concatenation level expands parallel encoded-resource width without increasing the protected online sequence length of these constructions. These results identify a modular route to lower logical error rates while retaining a common Gaussian MBQC operation set with shallow online processing.

items.title_en: Minimal unitary representations of time-invariant causal quantum channels
items.title_zh: 时不变因果量子信道的最小酉表示
items.abstract_en: In this work, we study quantum channels that respect causality in single-input-single-output linear time-invariant systems. We show that positive semidefinite kernels satisfying certain analyticity constraints, which we call Schur-class kernels, provide a suitable description of such channels through multiplicative maps (Schur multipliers). Using the Moore-Aronszajn Theorem, we establish that these multipliers admit a minimal analytic Stinespring representation, which, in the unital case, is given by multiplication by a left inner function. We then relate the output rank of pure-state inputs to the dimension of the associated reproducing kernel Hilbert space. Using de Branges-Rovnyak realizations, we derive a stability criterion for the existence of two-sided inner completions of these vector-valued functions. We further show that the adjoint of the Julia embedding associated with the realization is minimal, and that its characteristic function essentially coincides with the canonical two-sided inner completion suggested by the Beurling-Lax-Halmos Theorem. Finally, we provide algorithms for explicitly computing minimal two-sided inner completions in the case of finite McMillan degree.

items.title_en: Exploiting the Weyl-Chamber Structure for Hardware-Aware Quantum Circuit Compression
items.title_zh: 利用Weyl-Chamber结构进行硬件感知的量子电路压缩
items.abstract_en: Quantum circuit compression based on tensor networks enables long-time simulation of quantum many-body dynamics on near-term hardware. While Riemannian optimization has been successfully employed for this purpose, it typically optimizes over the manifold of generic two-qubit unitaries.
